page: Microsoft Azure D4ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC 9V45 cores with hyperthreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 236 GB NVMe SSD and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the AMD EPYC processor delivers top-tier single-core performance, as evidenced by its stress-ng single-core score and high single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression rates. However, multi-threaded scaling presents a notable tradeoff; multi-core stress-ng performance and passmark CPU scores fall into the average tier, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth remains average across both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks.

The resource profile of the D4ads_v7 offers balanced cost efficiency for general-purpose workloads that require a mix of compute, memory, and fast local storage without the premium of specialized hardware. It is well-suited for applications such as static web serving, database operations, and lightweight LLM inference on small models, where it maintains average throughput. Conversely, it is poorly suited for medium-to-large language model prompt processing due to low token-per-second performance.
